_plan.section_job: Convert the 2.1 framework into formal, falsifiable predictions about WHERE/WHEN the language signal appears -- never WHY. Each hypothesis: a prediction (direction + where/when) + the prior empirical contrast that makes it non-obvious, leaning on contrasts 2.1 already set up.
_plan.spine: P1 funnel -> P2 H1 (anticipatory run-up) -> P3 H1a (cash-concentration) -> P4 H1b (differential timing/two clocks) -> P5 scrutiny competing-hypothesis (the rival 4.1 rules out).
_plan.serves: Falsifiable claims with stakes; the bridge to the 2.4 designs (which map each design to a hypothesis).
_plan.boundary: Predictions only. Do NOT define the measure (2.3) or estimator (2.4); never assert a cause.
_plan.thin_claim: H1a = concentration not strict specificity; no hypothesis asserts a cause; the scrutiny alternative is a real competing hypothesis, not a strawman.
_plan.division_of_labor: 2.1 DEVELOPED both dimensions (P3 anticipatory, P5 cash + two clocks) and the contrasts (P6 thewissen/keown; P2 matsumoto). 2.2 ADDS only: formal falsifiable hypotheses + the scrutiny competing-hypothesis. It does NOT re-review any 2.1 paper.

P1.final_prose: The preceding section isolates two dimensions of the pattern we expect: an \emph{anticipatory} dimension, in which CEO uncertainty language is elevated while an acquisition remains undisclosed and recedes once it is announced, and a \emph{cash-concentrated} dimension, in which that elevation is stronger for cash acquisitions than for stock. This section turns those dimensions into formal, falsifiable predictions about \emph{where} and \emph{when} the signal appears in a CEO's unscripted answers---not why it appears, a mechanism the framework leaves open. The object of each prediction is the call-varying residual of CEO uncertainty language in the Q\&A---the component that remains once a CEO's persistent speaking style is netted out, which the next section defines formally---and every prediction is read in descriptive, correlational terms. Timing is measured in event time: $e$ counts calendar quarters relative to a firm's first acquisition announcement, so that $e=-1$ denotes the call in the quarter immediately before it. The focal pre-announcement indicator is $\mathrm{PreAnnounceQtr} = \mathbf{1}[e=-1]$, defined for a firm's first acquisition financed at least half in cash. The three hypotheses that follow---H1, H1a, and H1b---are stated here as predictions and confronted with the data by the designs developed below.

P4.boundary: Timing prediction only; no cause; no estimator.
P4.thin_claim: Round-trip contrast; do NOT over-read the negative POST overshoot.

GAP discriminator (C1 crux, advisor): the MNPI fingerprint is the DROP at the GAP bin (announced, NOT yet closed) -> uncertainty ~0 while cash still persists. Do NOT flatten GAP+POST into 'gone post' -- that loses the discriminator. (empire_drop_test: GAP = MNPI->~0 vs outcome->stays high.)

propositions.statement: H1b: residual Q&A uncertainty resolves at announcement -- dropping even before the deal closes (the GAP window: announced, not yet completed) -- while the acquirer's cash persists until it is paid at completion; the two run on different clocks.
propositions.role_in_paragraph: The differential-timing hypothesis statement; the GAP-vs-completion contrast IS H1b.
propositions.verification_plan: Prediction we TEST (claim C1). No NLM.

propositions.statement: The cash-persistence leg is partly mechanical (cash physically leaves at closing); and the post-announcement uncertainty undershoot is not to be over-read.
